question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To cost an arm and a leg

options.text: Someone does not have money to buy something

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"To cost an arm and a leg"** means something that is very expensive. (बहुत महंगा होना)

 
 
• **Example: **Buying a new car can cost an arm and a leg.
 
 
 
• **"Very expensive" **refers to something that requires a lot of money to buy or maintain. (बहुत महंगा)
 
 
• **Example: **His new house is very expensive, it cost him an arm and a leg.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Someone is badly hurt **(किसी को बुरी तरह चोट लगी है): Refers to someone who has sustained significant physical injuries.

 
 
• **Example:** He was badly hurt in the accident and needed immediate medical attention.
 
 
 
• **Someone has borne losses **(किसी ने नुकसान उठाया है): Refers to someone who has experienced financial or material loss.
 
 
• **Example: **He has borne heavy losses in the stock market.
 
 
 
• **Someone does not have money to buy something** (किसी के पास कुछ खरीदने के लिए पैसे नहीं हैं): Refers to someone who lacks the financial means to purchase something.
 
 
• **Example:** She does not have money to buy a new dress.
